prerequisites: Basic knowledge of logic and computer science.
Previous knowledge of programming languages is recommended but not mandatory.

learning_outcomes.text: The student will be able to understand and design the main components that form a web server.
The student will be able to use the necessary tools to create the components of a web server, both to identify solutions and to justify, support, and argue their design choices.

The student will be able to analyze and design basic web systems, considering criteria such as resource requests and system response speed, and to identify and gather additional information to achieve greater awareness if the acquired knowledge is insufficient to meet the required requirements.

The student will be able to present the functionalities of a web system and to communicate implementation issues related to the design and resource availability required for implementing a web system.

The student will be able to evaluate and recognize the acquired knowledge and to search for additional solutions through bibliographic research to pursue further studies, such as master's degree courses.

syllabus_topics: Static Web Programming: HTML and CSS
Dynamic Web Programming: JavaScript and PHP/Python
Database and storage: SQL and CRUD operations
Responsive sites and Grid Management with Bootstrap
Exercises and refining the full product

assessment_methods.method: Oral test (theoretical questions and design exercises)
Development of a group software project

assessment_rules: The assessment test consists of two phases: an oral test and the development of a group software project. The oral test contributes to 2/3 of the final grade, and the group software project contributes to 1/3. To pass the exam, the student must receive a score of no less than 18/30. The test is evaluated with a maximum score of 32, with honors awarded if the score is greater than or equal to 31.
bibliography: The texts and teaching materials will be provided through the course web page.
